close_reason:
Applied standard Rust sealed-trait pattern to all three public extension traits:
- JmapChatExt (lib.rs) — sealed over jmap_base_client::JmapClient
- ChatSessionExt (session.rs) — sealed over jmap_base_client::Session
- ChatWsExt (ws.rs) — sealed over jmap_base_client::WsSession

Each trait gets a private 'mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} impl Sealed for ...; }' adjacent to its declaration, and gains 'Sealed' as a supertrait bound. Trait rustdoc updated with a paragraph noting the sealing and its rationale (prevents downstream divergence + keeps adding methods non-breaking).

Zero impact on intended single-impl case. External downstream that did NOT already impl any of the three traits is source-compatible. cargo test, clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc all green. Committed as b9e4c70.
description:
Files:
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/lib.rs:56-61 (`JmapChatExt`)
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/session.rs:112-168 (`ChatSessionExt`)
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/ws.rs:77-108 (`ChatWsExt`)

All three traits are declared without the standard sealed-trait pattern (private supertrait or `Sealed` marker). The crate provides exactly one impl per trait:
- `impl JmapChatExt for jmap_base_client::JmapClient` (lib.rs:63)
- `impl ChatSessionExt for jmap_base_client::Session` (session.rs)
- `impl ChatWsExt for jmap_base_client::WsSession` (ws.rs:110)

Caller impact: a downstream crate can write `impl JmapChatExt for MyCustomThing` and break the design intent (these are extension traits over specific types, not capability traits). Once any downstream relies on its own impl, fixing the missing-seal becomes a breaking change.

Adding a method to any of these traits is also currently a breaking change for downstream impls — sealing eliminates that surface.

The Rust pattern is well-known: declare a private `mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} impl Sealed for jmap_base_client::JmapClient {} }`, then make the public trait extend `sealed::Sealed`. Add the impl line for each of the three target types in each respective module.

Cost: ~5 lines per trait, no API surface change for the intended single-impl case, prevents downstream divergence and future trait-method-add breakage.
title: Three public traits not sealed: callers can impl outside crate
